paper.title: STELLA: Self-Evolving LLM Agent for Biomedical Research
paper.central_claim: STELLA, a multi-agent biomedical research agent with an evolving Template Library and a Tool Ocean grown by a Tool Creation Agent, reaches state-of-the-art benchmark accuracy and improves systematically with experience.

gap.author_gap: Biomedical AI agents rely on manually curated, static toolsets and cannot keep pace with the field; a self-evolving agent should discover tools and update its knowledge from experience.
gap.checked_gap: The static-toolset limitation is plausible but asserted with citations only; the paper does not show that tool coverage limits the baselines (no tool-set ablation or failure attribution), and general self-evolving-agent neighbors (skill/tool libraries, experience memories) are not discussed.

rs_pattern.reason: Executed operation: a Manager decomposes, a Dev agent emits executable Python run in conda environments, a Critic loops on intermediate results, and a Tool Creation agent builds tools for capability gaps (decompose_and_delegate / C25, matching the r01a OS-Copilot and cal-h1 LATM rulings for tool-forging systems). The Template Library adds a weakly specified conditioning channel (adapt_via_conditioning, sub null).

claims.baseline_control: Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude 4 Opus, DeepSeek-R1, o3, Biomni
claims.selection_vs_test: no development set; trials on scored items
claims.result_denominator: 50 questions on HLE; subset sizes not stated; 3 runs
claims.allowed_conclusion: Task-level scores on small benchmark subsets exceed those of the listed single-pass models under the authors protocol.

claims.text: Performance systematically improves with experience (HLE-Bio 14% to 26%), evidencing self-evolution.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Accuracy rises with number of trials; attribution to retained templates or tools is not established.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Accuracy rises with the number of trials (1×→9×) averaged over three runs, but nothing isolates retained templates or tools from repeated sampling or retry; no store-off or equal-trial control.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported, figure-only values: with up to 9× trials and a Claude 4 Sonnet + Gemini 2.5 Pro multi-agent setup, STELLA scores higher than listed single-pass LLMs and Biomni on a 50-question HLE-Biomedicine set and 12.5% LAB-Bench subsets, and accuracy rises with trials. The author claim that the self-evolving Template Library / Tool Ocean causes the improvement is not supported by any isolating evidence. Not reproduced.
unresolved: Trial protocol and answer aggregation undefined (opus:O01).
Whether ground-truth correctness feeds template/tool storage between trials.
No template/tool ablation, equal-trial baseline, cost or held-out set.
